hypothesis: Projecting existing trajectory diagnostics into typed process-discipline records will make autonomy and harness quality comparisons more inspectable without replacing outcome gates or rollout decisions.

metricsCompared.name: process-discipline rubric coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: trajectory diagnostics exposed warning counts but no typed per-dimension process-discipline record
metricsCompared.candidate: focused tests cover clean, missing verification, repeated failure, edit-after-pass, unsupported stream, and blocked/no-op abstention evidence

metricsCompared.name: operator report visibility
metricsCompared.baseline: kota report did not expose grouped process-discipline scores
metricsCompared.candidate: report aggregation, rendering, and JSON smoke tests expose grouped process-discipline records without cost or raw-output fields

metricsCompared.name: rollout evidence depth
metricsCompared.baseline: no score existed for live-window harness or workflow comparison
metricsCompared.candidate: advisory score exists with local deterministic tests, but no multi-run live comparison has been accumulated yet

rationale: The implementation adds an advisory operator-report signal backed by deterministic local tests and existing trajectory artifacts. It does not make the score a pass/fail gate or promote any harness, reviewer, prompt, or workflow route; live-window comparisons should accumulate before relying on this score for rollout decisions.
